Full summary: Implemented #32 and #42: registry auto-touch on every post/decide/record write (unknown skipped, historical agents never expunged), and dashboard single-instance guard (same-project probe across the retry window before binding; second instance stays MCP-only).
Decisions: Chose engine-level registry auto-touch via BlackboardEngine.touchAgent (setter-injected IAgentStore, reused by DecisionEngine through its blackboardEngine reference) over per-tool touches — one implementation covers post/decide/record and any future write path; fire-and-forget so a registry failure never fails a write.; Chose to skip registry auto-touch for agent_id 'unknown' — a shared record would aggregate unrelated identity-less callers into noise; follows the subagent-stop-hook silence precedent (decision 01KWNSPM43J8D0SSGXNV37H7RB).; Chose to keep TTL-derived liveness purely as display status with no expunge — already structurally true (liveness computed from last_active, twining_agents include_gone defaults true), so #32's TTL concern needed documentation, not code.; Chose a pre-bind same-project probe across the full port retry window (config.port..+5) for the #42 single-instance guard, reusing the existing /api/health projectRoot check — probing only the configured port would miss a first instance that was itself bumped by a foreign occupant; a different project's dashboard still falls through to the existing next-port retry.; Chose to ship the #42 guard without the ${TWINING_MCP_CMD} env-expansion escape hatch — the hatch depends on upstream claude-code#9427 behavior that can only be verified in a live plugin context; noted as follow-up on the issue rather than shipping unverified.
Findings: BEHAVIORS.md is machine-parsed by the eval harness with a schema requiring workflow-step tools to start with twining_ — prose steps like '(write + commit doc)' break test/eval/behaviors-parser.test.ts; keep workflow tables tool-shaped.
